source.title: MCP server OAuth puts N8N_PATH value at the end rather than at the front

source.body:
### Bug Description

Title: Native MCP OAuth discovery fails when n8n is mounted under N8N_PATH=/somepath/

Describe the bug

I feel like this is a bug, but it may also be intended. But if it is intended, it doesn't really make sense to me. We run n8n self hosted behind a reverse proxy. Our reverse proxy routes based on path. For example /somepath. To accomodate this, n8n has the N8N_PATH env var. But this ends up with an advertises protected-resource url of https://example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/somepath/mcp-server/http. This doesn't fit the reverse proxy's routing rule. I would expect the url to be https://example.com/somepath/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp-server/http. So I think there's an issue with the URL construction.

#### EDIT: the consent url /oauth/consent also does not respect N8N_PATH at all.

### To Reproduce

To reproduce
1. Set N8N_PATH=/somepath/ and N8N_EDITOR_BASE_URL=https://example.com/somepath/. Enable instance-level MCP and route /somepath/* to n8n.
2. Send an unauthenticated HEAD request to https://example.com/somepath/mcp-server/http. n8n returns the expected 401 and advertises:
   https://example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/somepath/mcp-server/http
3. Send a GET to that advertised URL. It falls through to the default backend instead of returning metadata.
4. Send a GET to https://example.com/somepath/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/somepath/mcp-server/http. It returns 200 with JSON, and the resource field matches https://example.com/somepath/mcp-server/http.
Expected behavior


### Expected behavior

The URL in WWW-Authenticate: resource_metadata=… should return metadata JSON for the MCP endpoint. The advertised URL follows [RFC 9728 §3.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9728.html#section-3.1); the issue is that the document is served at a different path. If subpath installs require an explicit root-level proxy route, please document it in the native MCP setup instructions.

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: I traced the discovery URL to `McpProtectedResource.getProtectedResourceMetadataUrl()` in `packages/cli/src/modules/mcp/mcp-protected-resource.ts`. It builds the URL from `url.origin` plus `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and `url.pathname`, so a base-path prefix on the resource URL is placed after `.well-known` instead of before it. That matches the mismatch in your reproduction. Preserving the instance mount prefix in the well-known route, with a regression case for a non-root `N8N_PATH`, should cover the `WWW-Authenticate` metadata URL; the `/oauth/consent` path would need its own check.

Hey @jelleholtkamp. I reproduced this issue and it came out to be valid. N8N_PATH is a public URL prefix only: n8n mounts routes at /, and the reverse proxy strips /somepath before forwarding. Today:
- Metadata URL is built as origin/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/<full path>, so with N8N_PATH=/somepath it advertises https://example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/somepath/mcp-server/http. That URL is outside the proxy's /somepath route and is unreachable.
- Consent redirect is root-relative: /oauth/consent?flow=…, so it drops the public path too.
- The same metadata-URL construction is duplicated in MCP, the bearer driver, and the workflow OAuth helper.
